    Band bricks of shape P ω Q ω⁻¹ #

    Plamondon's second family: a cyclic word P ++ ω ++ Q ++ ω⁻¹ where P and Q are closed walks whose own junctions fail alternation, with the same direction type at their ends. Positions with the same vertex are mirror positions across ω; their halves agree along ω and first differ at the ends of P and of Q, and the same direction type makes one of the two comparisons refute the plus-set condition. Hence the band modules are bricks (isBrick_shape2).

    theorem BrickAccessibility.CWord.shape_A1 {k : Type u} [Field k] {B : Type u} [Ring B] [Algebra k B] {D : MonomialData k B} (b : CWord D.Q) {P ω Q : List (Letter D.Q)} (hc : b.letters = P ++ ω ++ Q ++ invLetters ω) (hP : P ≠ []) (hQ : Q ≠ []) (i : ℕ) (hi : i ≤ ω.length) :
    have a := ⟨P.length + i, ⋯⟩; have a' := ⟨(b.n - i) % b.n, ⋯⟩; (∀ t < ω.length - i, b.rightW a t = b.leftW a' t) ∧ b.rightW a (ω.length - i) = Q.head hQ ∧ b.leftW a' (ω.length - i) = (Q.getLast hQ).inv

    The forward half from |P| + i and the backward half from its mirror.
